tasks.source: questions.json questions[0] exact stem/options; publisher extract only; official correspondence not established.
derivation: For the standard ideal particle model in which P is the net rate of increase of translational kinetic energy, d(mv^2/2)/dt=P. With initial rest, v(t)=sqrt(2Pt/m) on the positive-going branch.

A shorter exact-MCQ route eliminates B/C by units, leaving x=c*t^(3/2). Differentiate: v=(3/2)c*t^(1/2), a=(3/4)c*t^(-1/2); P=mva=(9/8)m*c^2. Only D has the required coefficient. No full quadrature is required to select it.
conditions_and_limits: P>0,m>0,t>=0 and positive x orientation. The formula is a limiting ideal solution: a and F=P/v diverge as t approaches0+; no finite-force engine literally supplies constant positive mechanical power at exactly rest. This does not change the ideal t>0 answer.

Engine output equals net translational power only if losses/drag, rotational energy and other energy channels are neglected or included in a suitable net P. They are not specified in the source; if literal engine output with unknown losses is demanded, x(t) is not uniquely determined. This is a conditional idealization, not a source repair or difficulty point.
checks: Units: sqrt(P/m)*t^(3/2) has units of length. x(0)=v(0)=0 in the limiting sense. Substitution into mva returns P.
Isolated numeric substitution P=7,m=3,t=2 gave mva=6.999999999999998 against P=7.

primary_operation.reason: Executing the familiar power relation on candidate x(t) decides this exact MCQ; the derivative check is a valid short route.
primary_operation.competing: SYNTHESIZE (columns.6): power -> kinetic energy -> speed -> position is a legitimate longer construction, but the exact options allow routine relation checking without a nontrivial bridge/order decision. It does not support a D3 synthesis claim.
primary_operation.evidence_limit: columns.3.evidence_criterion additionally requires applicability, mapping and check; selecting D alone does not supply that learner evidence.

tasks.source: questions.json questions[1]; publisher extract only; official correspondence not established.
tasks.answer: C for the minimum/ideal lifting work: MgL/(2n^2).
derivation: Let hanging length ell=L/n and uniform line density M/L. Hanging mass is M/n; its centre of mass starts ell/2 below the tabletop.
Raising that mass to the tabletop increases gravitational potential energy by (M/n)*g*(L/(2n))=MgL/(2n^2).
Independent distributed check: integrate (M/L)*g*y dy from0 to L/n, giving MgL/(2n^2). No variable-force integration is necessary for the shortest route.
conditions_and_limits: M,L>0 and n>=1 so the stated fraction is physically possible. Uniformity is explicit and makes the COM halfway down.

The gravitational energy increase is fixed by the endpoints. Equality to external lifting work requires no dissipative work and equal initial/final kinetic energies (usually quasi-static). An unspecified rough tabletop, pulling motion or final speed can increase the required external work. Source conditions are empty, so an unconditional external-work equality is not established. No friction model is silently added.

The conventional ideal question is usable conditionally; no intrinsic algebraic contradiction or necessary repair was found. If its intended quantity is total agent work in an unspecified dissipative process, literal task is underdetermined and that claim is HOLD.
checks: For n=1 this is MgL/2, the work raising a fully hanging uniform length by its half-length COM distance. For n -> infinity it tends to0 quadratically.
Midpoint distributed-work sum with M=9,L=4,n=3,g=10 and10000 slices gave19.999999999999993, agreeing with COM result20.

tasks.source: questions.json questions[2]; publisher extract only; official correspondence not established.
derivation: For initially unstretched ideal Hooke-law springs, elastic work to extension x is W=k*x^2/2. In terms of the common final force F=kx it is W=F^2/(2k).
At common F, the premise W1>W2 implies1/k1>1/k2, hence k1<k2. Statement2 is true.
At common extension x, W1/W2=k1/k2<1. Statement1 says the reverse and is false. No explanation-choice discrimination between optionsC/D is needed once Statement1 is refuted.
conditions_and_limits: Positive k values, ideal Hookean elastic regime and work measured from the same unstretched reference. The standard force comparison means a common final stretching force in the elastic-work relation. If actual force histories/initial strains differ, extra information would be needed; that alternative is not silently substituted.
The statement format alone does not demand a formal proof, causal explanation or D3/D4 reasoning.
checks: Concrete counterexample to Statement1: k1=2,k2=8,F=4 gives work4 and1; at common extension3 gives work9 and36. Both the premise and Statement2 hold while Statement1 fails.

tasks.source: original-saved-crop.png and official-paper.pdf printed page15 Q57; paper page1 instructions6-7.
tasks.answer: All four alternatives a,b,c,d are true on the stated conservative motion.
tasks.task_transcription: U(x)=alpha/x^2-beta/x; alpha,beta>0; released from rest at x0=alpha/beta. (a) U=(alpha/x0^2)*[(x0/x)^2-x0/x]; (b) v=sqrt((2alpha/(m*x0^2))*[x0/x-(x0/x)^2]); (c) vmax=sqrt(alpha/(2m*x0^2)); (d) KE+U=0.
derivation: Since beta=alpha/x0, substituting in U establishes(a). At x0, U=0; initial v=0, so conserved total energy E=0 and(d) follows.

The force F=-dU/dx=2alpha/x^3-beta/x^2 is positive at release: F(x0)=alpha/x0^3>0. The particle moves right. Its allowed connected region is x>=x0, with no finite right-hand turning point; it cannot cross x=0.

Energy gives v^2=-2U/m=(2alpha/(m*x0^2))*[x0/x-(x0/x)^2]. The positive square root is velocity, not merely speed, because the particle moves right for every finite x>x0; hence(b) holds on the physical trajectory.

Let y=x0/x. On the physical region0<y<=1, y-y^2=1/4-(y-1/2)^2 has maximum1/4 at y=1/2, i.e.x=2x0. Thus vmax^2=alpha/(2m*x0^2), giving(c). This direct square-completion route avoids a lengthy force-time solution.
conditions_and_limits: m>0; autonomous conservative potential with standard F=-dU/dx, no additional nonconservative forces. x=0 is singular, but initial x0>0 fixes the connected accessible branch.

The displayed positive-root v(x) is valid on this released trajectory. Arbitrary left-moving initial data would require a negative branch; those are not the given task. At x -> infinity, v approaches0; no finite return occurs.
All-correct is expressly allowed by the original A-2 instructions. Treating this as single-correct would manufacture a source flaw. No official key was consulted or authenticated.
checks: At x=x0, U=v=0. At x=2x0, U=-alpha/(4x0^2); maximum speed follows directly from K=-U. At infinity, U and v approach0 consistently with E=0.

Isolated values alpha=18,beta=6,m=2 gave x0=3,E0=0,F0=2/3; U(6)=-0.5 and vmax=0.7071067811865476 from both formulas. Option(a) identity tested at four x values with maximum floating discrepancy2.78e-17. Numeric examples check implementation only; analytic derivation establishes the claims.

But direct energy substitution and square completion are sufficient for the exact option set; it lacks a nontrivial stage-order/model coordination bottleneck.
